mainTopic: Vows a husband makes or allows that harm his wife: adornment, visiting her father, and going to mourners or celebrations
overview: The amud opens by explaining a source about a wife who vows not to adorn herself. First the גמרא says the case is about דברים שבינו לבינה. That answer only fits רב הונא, not רב אדא בר אהבה, so the גמרא gives a new answer: she tied her adornment to תשמיש המטה, following רב כהנא's rule. Then it asks why she can't just skip adorning (people would call her repulsive), and why he can't keep her for a week or two (his silence makes her think he hates her). Next, the גמרא explains רבי יוסי's time limits for poor and wealthy women. A new משנה follows about a husband who bans his wife from her father's house, from a בית האבל or בית המשתה, or who sets humiliating conditions. אביי and רבה בר עולא each resolve a contradiction in the time limits about festivals. After two teachings of רבי יוחנן about a bride, the גמרא returns to the משנה. It begins a question about the house of feasting that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case is about private matters between husband and wife
steps.stepSummary: The challenge from before ends with "colored garments." The גמרא answers that our case is about a vow touching דברים שבינו לבינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [...the source spoke of] colored garments! The answer: here we are dealing with matters that are between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: The first word closes the question from before. Then the גמרא answers by placing the vow about adornment in the category of דברים שבינו לבינה, which a husband can nullify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that refusing adornment seems to affect only the wife, so why can the husband nullify it? The answer moves the vow into a different category: private matters of the marriage. That category also gives a husband the power of הפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (a formula that narrows the case)
Matters between him and her: private parts of married life

steps.confusionAlert: The first word, "with colored garments!", is not part of the answer. It is the last word of the question from the previous lines.

phrases.english: with colored garments!
Here, with what are we dealing?
With matters that are between him and her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that closes with "colored garments"
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The adornment vow affects only her, so the husband should have no power to nullify it
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow concerns דברים שבינו לבינה, which the husband can nullify

steps.title: That answer only fits one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the answer works for whoever holds that a husband can nullify vows about דברים שבינו לבינה. What about the opinion that he cannot?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says that in matters between him and her the husband can nullify. But for the one who says the husband cannot nullify, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. That answer depends on one side of a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 1 assumes that vows about דברים שבינו לבינה can be nullified. Some hold they cannot. For them the source is still unexplained, so the גמרא wants an answer that works for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: This is fine according to the one who says...
What is there to say? (the answer doesn't work)

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who said
that in matters between him and her, the husband can nullify.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין הַבַּעַל מֵיפֵר,
phrases.english: But according to the one who said the husband cannot nullify,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case concerns דברים שבינו לבינה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer only fits one side of a known disagreement, so it fails for the other side

steps.title: The disagreement between רב הונא and רב אדא בר אהבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the disagreement it mentioned. רב הונא says the husband can nullify vows about דברים שבינו לבינה. רב אדא בר אהבה says he cannot, using a picture of a fox.
steps.simpleTranslation: For it was stated: about matters between him and her, רב הונא says the husband can nullify. רב אדא בר אהבה says the husband cannot nullify, because we never found a fox that died from the dirt of its own hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its question by quoting the actual disagreement between the אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה holds that this kind of vow does not truly harm the husband. Just as a fox is used to the dirt of its own hole, a husband is used to his wife. That is why, in his view, the vow is not something the husband can nullify.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a disagreement between אמוראים)
The dirt of a hole or den

phrases.english: As it was stated: matters that are between him and her,
Rav Huna said: the husband can nullify,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר: אֵין הַבַּעַל מֵיפֵר,
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said: the husband cannot nullify,
for we have not found a fox
that died from the dirt of its hole.
phrases.notes: It's a picture: the fox is used to its own hole, and the husband is used to his wife, so it won't harm him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the source of the disagreement the question relied on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: a husband can nullify vows about דברים שבינו לבינה. רב אדא בר אהבה: he cannot, since he is not harmed.

steps.title: A new answer: she tied her adornment to intimacy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives an answer that works for everyone. She vowed that the pleasure of תשמיש המטה with her husband would be forbidden to her if she adorned herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here we are dealing with a case where she made her adornment depend on marital intimacy. She said: "May the pleasure of intimacy with you be forbidden to me if I adorn myself," as רב כהנא said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first answer and gives a new one. It also sets up a quote from רב כהנא, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the vow is not only about not adorning herself. If she adorns herself, intimacy itself becomes forbidden. That directly affects the marriage, so everyone agrees the husband can nullify it.

keyTerms.meaning: She made them hang on (made one depend on the other)
The pleasure of intimacy with you

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer no longer depends on the disagreement between רב הונא and רב אדא בר אהבה.

phrases.english: Rather, here, with what are we dealing?
For example, where she made her adornments depend
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected spelling. Read it as "she made them hang on."

phrases.english: on marital intimacy,
that she said: "May the pleasure of intimacy with you be forbidden to me
if I adorn myself,"
as Rav Kahana said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of step 1 in response to the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: New case definition (אוקימתא) acceptable to all opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case was only about adornment as a private matter, which works for רב הונא alone
steps.terutzMaskana: She linked adornment to the prohibition of intimacy, so all agree the husband can nullify

steps.title: רב כהנא's rule about vows on intimacy
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא separates two wordings. If she forbids herself to him, he can force her, because she has no power over what she owes him. If she forbids him to herself, he cannot force her, because we don't feed a person something forbidden to him. Instead he may nullify the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: if she says "the pleasure of intimacy with me is forbidden to you," he compels her and she is intimate with him. If she says "the pleasure of intimacy with you is forbidden to me," he should nullify it, because we do not feed a person something that is forbidden to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב כהנא's rule in full to support the answer in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first wording, she tries to take away what she owes her husband, and that vow has no power over him. In the second wording, she forbids her own pleasure. That vow takes hold on her, so he cannot just force her. The way out is for him to nullify it. This is why the vow in step 4, phrased as "intimacy with you is forbidden to me," is one the husband nullifies.

keyTerms.term: אֵין מַאֲכִילִין לָאָדָם דָּבָר הָאָסוּר לוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: We do not feed a person something forbidden to him

steps.whatToRemember: Wording matters. "Me to you": he can compel her. "You to me": he cannot compel her, but he can nullify the vow. A vow to avoid adornment that is tied to intimacy in the "you to me" form is one every opinion agrees the husband can nullify.
steps.confusionAlert: The two wordings sound almost the same, but they flip who is forbidden. In the first she forbids herself to him. In the second she forbids him to herself.

phrases.english: For Rav Kahana said:
"The pleasure of intimacy with me is upon you"
he compels her, and she is intimate with him.
"The pleasure of intimacy with you is upon me"
he should nullify,
because one does not feed a person
something that is forbidden to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source cited at the end of step 4
steps.raayaObject: That a vow forbidding the husband's intimacy to herself is one the husband nullifies
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With the "you to me" wording, he cannot force her, so he nullifies the vow.

steps.title: Why not just skip adorning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 4: if the prohibition only starts when she adorns herself, she can simply not adorn herself and never be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let her not adorn herself, and then she won't be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the case it set up in Step 4. If she just doesn't adorn herself, the vow never takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 the vow was conditional: תשמיש המטה is forbidden only if she adorns herself. The challenge says she can easily avoid the condition, so the ban on intimacy never takes effect. What is left is just a vow not to adorn herself, and that alone is not something the husband can nullify.

phrases.english: Let her not adorn herself, and she will not be forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conditional-vow case set up in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case from Step 4: a vow making תשמיש המטה forbidden if she adorns herself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The condition can be avoided, so the vow never has to take effect and needs no cancelling.

steps.title: People would call her repulsive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that she cannot really go without adorning, because people would call her repulsive.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, they will call her 'repulsive.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 6: not adorning isn't a real option for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who never adorns herself would be shamed and called repulsive. So in practice she will adorn herself at some point, and the vow will take effect. That makes it a real vow about their life together.

phrases.english: If so, they will call her "repulsive."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: the condition can't really be avoided.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She can simply avoid adorning and the vow never applies.
steps.terutzMaskana: Going without adornment would shame her, so she will adorn and the vow will take effect.

steps.title: Why not keep her for a week or two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: let her adorn and be forbidden. We know from בית שמאי and בית הלל that a marriage can last a while with such a ban, so why divorce right away?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let her adorn herself and be forbidden! Like the rule we know: according to בית שמאי, two weeks; according to בית הלל, one week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge. In the case of a husband who forbids relations by a vow, he may stay married for a short time, so why not here too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה taught that when a husband vows to forbid relations with his wife, he can keep her for two weeks (בית שמאי) or one week (בית הלל). So a short ban on relations does not force an immediate divorce. Why should her vow be any different?

phrases.english: So let her adorn herself and be forbidden,
if according to בית שמאי, two weeks,
phrases.notes: This points to the earlier משנה about a husband who vows to forbid relations with his wife.

phrases.english: if according to בית הלל, one week!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that she will adorn, then asks why he can't keep her for a limited time.
steps.kashyaTarget: The demand that he must cancel the vow or divorce her right away.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the husband-vow case the law allows a week or two of marriage under such a ban, so the same should apply here.

steps.title: His silence tells her he hates her
steps.stepSummary: The week-or-two rule applies only when he made the vow, since she thinks he is just angry. Here she vowed and he stayed silent, so she concludes he hates her.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only where he made the vow. She thinks: 'He got angry at me, and now he will calm down.' But here, she vowed and he stayed silent. She thinks: 'Since he is silent, he must hate me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 8 by showing the two cases are different in how the wife feels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband vows, she sees it as a moment of anger that will pass, so she can wait a week or two. When she vows and he could cancel it but says nothing, his silence sends a message: he doesn't care for her. That hurts the marriage, so he must cancel or divorce.
steps.whatToRemember: A husband's own vow looks like passing anger; his silence over her vow looks like hatred. That difference is why her vow forces an immediate decision.

phrases.english: This applies only where he made her forbidden by a vow,
because she thinks: He is angry at me,
and soon he will calm down.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דִּנְדַרָה אִיהִי וְשָׁתֵיק לַהּ,
phrases.english: But here, where she vowed and he stayed silent toward her,
she thinks: since he kept silent,
he must truly hate me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by separating the husband-vow case from this wife-vow case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the wife's understanding.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any ban on relations can last a week or two before divorce.
steps.terutzMaskana: That grace period is only when he vowed; when she vowed and he kept silent, she reads it as hatred.

steps.title: רבי יוסי on poor women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי from the משנה: for poor women, he must divorce if he did not set a time limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: For poor women, when he did not set a time limit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the next line of the משנה to explain it. This sets up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says that for poor women, a ban on adorning forces divorce only if no time limit was set. If he set a limit, he may keep her. The גמרא will now ask how long that limit can be.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says:
For poor women, when he did not set a time limit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For poor women, he must divorce only if he set no time limit.

steps.title: How long can the limit be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a time limit is allowed for poor women.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long is the time limit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי יוסי's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A time limit can't be endless, or it is just like no limit at all. The גמרא wants to know the longest limit that still lets him keep her.

phrases.english: And how long is the time limit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of קצבה in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum length of the time limit for poor women.

steps.title: Three opinions on the limit
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says twelve months, רבי יוחנן says ten years, and אבימי says until the next רגל, since Jewish women adorn themselves on the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: twelve months. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: ten years. רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: a רגל, because Jewish women adorn themselves on the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three different answers to the question in Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each answer sets a different maximum length. אבימי gives a reason: on a רגל women adorn themselves, so a ban that lasts past it is too much for her. Poor women are used to adorning less, which is why the limit can be fairly long.

keyTerms.meaning: one of the three pilgrimage festivals

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
Twelve months.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
Ten years.
רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: a festival,
phrases.notes: He means until the next of the three festivals (פסח, שבועות, סוכות).

phrases.english: because Jewish women adorn themselves on the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11 with three opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Twelve months (שמואל), ten years (רבי יוחנן), or until the next רגל (אבימי).

steps.title: רבי יוסי on wealthy women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rest of רבי יוסי's words: for wealthy women, the limit is thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for wealthy women, thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second half of רבי יוסי's statement. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wealthy women are used to adorning themselves, so the allowed time is much shorter. If the ban lasts more than thirty days, he must divorce her.

phrases.english: And for wealthy women, thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting רבי יוסי's words from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For wealthy women, the ban may last up to thirty days.

steps.title: Why exactly thirty days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is special about thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the number thirty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number seems random. The גמרא wants to know why the limit for wealthy women is exactly thirty days.

phrases.english: What is different about thirty days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the limit for wealthy women is thirty days.

steps.title: The scent lasts thirty days
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that an important woman still enjoys the scent of her earlier adornments for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because an important woman enjoys the scent of her adornments for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question of Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The perfume and adornments she already put on keep their scent for about thirty days. During that time she still feels cared for and attractive. After that she feels repulsive, so the ban can't go longer.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's limits depend on what the woman is used to: long limits for poor women, only thirty days for wealthy women, matching how long the scent of her adornments lasts.

phrases.english: אביי said:
Because an important woman enjoys
the scent of her adornments for thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The scent of her earlier adornments lasts thirty days, so she doesn't feel neglected until then.

steps.title: Vowing that his wife may not visit her father's house
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a husband's vow keeps his wife from her father's house, a short ban is allowed but a long one forces divorce with payment of the כתובה. The time limit depends on whether her father lives in the same city or in a different city.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man made a vow forbidding his wife to go to her father's house. If her father lives in the same city, he may keep her if the ban lasts one month. If it lasts two months, he must divorce her and pay her כתובה. If her father lives in another city, he may keep her if the ban lasts one רגל. If it lasts three, he must divorce her and pay her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets time limits on how long a husband may keep his wife from visiting her father's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping a wife from her family is treated as a real harm to her, but a small harm she can be expected to live with. In the same city, she would visit often, so the limit is measured in months. In a far city, she would only visit on the רגלים, so the limit is measured in festivals.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין: 'our משנה'. It marks the start of the משנה text.
One who makes a vow that forbids something to someone else (here, to his wife).
He may keep her (stay married to her).
He must divorce her and pay her the כתובה money.
One of the three pilgrimage festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who makes a vow forbidding his wife
so that she may not go to her father's house
when he is with her in the same city
phrases.notes: 'He' here means her father: he lives in the same city she does.

phrases.english: for one month, he may keep her
for two months, he must divorce her and give her the כתובה
and when he is in a different city
for one festival, he may keep her
for three festivals, he must divorce her and give her the כתובה

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא תֵּלֵךְ לְבֵית אָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the earlier discussion of time limits for vows about adornment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same city: one month is allowed, two months forces divorce with כתובה. Different city: one רגל is allowed, three forces divorce with כתובה.

steps.title: Vowing that his wife may not go to a house of mourning or a wedding feast
steps.stepSummary: A husband who bans his wife from going to a בית האבל or a בית המשתה must divorce her and pay the כתובה, because he is shutting her off from people. If he has a real other reason, he is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man who vows that his wife may not go to a house of mourning or a house of feasting must divorce her and pay her כתובה, because he is locking the door in her face. But if he claims he did it for some other reason, he is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: banning his wife from visiting mourners or going to celebrations. This ban forces a divorce right away, with no time limit given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is that this cuts her off from her community. If she never comforts others or joins their שמחות, others will not come to her either. But if the husband has a real concern about what goes on at that place, he is not 'locking her out', so he is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A house of mourning, where people go to comfort mourners.
A house of feasting, such as a wedding celebration.
Locking (the door) in her face; cutting her off from others.

phrases.english: One who makes a vow forbidding his wife
so that she may not go to a house of mourning
or to a house of feasting
must divorce her and give her the כתובה
because he is locking the door in her face

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיָה טוֹעֵן מִשּׁוּם דָּבָר אַחֵר
phrases.english: And if he was claiming it is because of something else
phrases.notes: He means a real concern about improper behavior going on at that place.

phrases.english: he is permitted

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא תֵּלֵךְ לְבֵית הָאֵבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second clause of the same משנה: another kind of vow that keeps the wife from going somewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Banning her from a בית האבל or a בית המשתה forces divorce with כתובה, unless he has a real other reason.

steps.title: Humiliating conditions for cancelling the vow
steps.stepSummary: If the husband says the vow will be cancelled only if she says certain embarrassing things, or does something shameful or pointless, he must divorce her and pay the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said to her: 'The vow is cancelled on condition that you tell so-and-so what you told me,' or 'what I told you,' or on condition that she fill something up and pour it out onto the garbage heap, he must divorce her and pay her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third set of cases: the husband attaches a degrading condition to cancelling his vow. All of these force a divorce with payment of the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the harm is not that she is kept from going somewhere. The harm is that the only way out of the vow is to embarrass herself or do something that looks foolish. The משנה lists the cases without explaining them; the גמרא will explain them later.

keyTerms.meaning: She fills up and pours out.

phrases.english: If he said to her: 'On condition
that you tell so-and-so what you told me'
or: 'what I told you'
or that she must fill something up and pour it out onto the garbage heap
he must divorce her and give her the כתובה

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתֹּאמְרִי לִפְלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third clause of the same משנה: degrading conditions for cancelling a vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making the cancellation of the vow depend on shameful words or actions forces divorce with כתובה.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three parts: (1) banning visits to her father, with time limits; (2) banning her from a בית האבל or a בית המשתה, which forces divorce unless he has a real reason; (3) humiliating conditions, which force divorce.

steps.title: The first clause seems to contradict itself about two festivals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that 'one רגל he may keep her' implies that two forces a divorce. But 'three, he must divorce' implies that two is still allowed. So what is the law for two?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This משנה contradicts itself. You said that for one festival he may keep her. That implies that for two he must divorce her and pay the כתובה. But look at the end of the clause: for three he must divorce her and pay the כתובה. That implies that for two he may keep her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out that the first part of the משנה gives two clashing messages about a ban lasting two festivals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one festival were the upper limit, the משנה should have said 'two, he must divorce.' If three is where divorce starts, then two should still be fine. The משנה skipped the number two, so each half of the sentence implies the opposite ruling for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא: marks the start of the גמרא's discussion.
'This itself is difficult': the text contradicts itself.
'Say the end part': now look at the later words of the text.

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is only about the festival case in a different city. It is not about the one-month or two-month case in the same city, where the משנה clearly says what happens at two.

phrases.english: GEMARA: This itself is difficult
phrases.notes: The problem is inside the משנה itself, not a clash with some other source.

phrases.english: You said: for one festival he may keep her
this implies that for two, he must divorce her and give the כתובה
Now say the end of the clause
for three, he must divorce her and give the כתובה
this implies that for two, he may keep her

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first comment on the משנה, aimed at the festival part of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the first clause of the משנה: one רגל is allowed, three forces divorce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading the beginning and the end of the clause by implication gives opposite rulings for two festivals: the beginning implies divorce, the end implies he may keep her.

steps.title: אביי: The later clause is about a כהן's wife, following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the 'three רגלים' clause is talking about a כהנת, and it follows the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In the later clause, we are dealing with the wife of a כהן, and it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction from step 19. He says the two clauses are about two different women: the 'three רגלים' clause is about a כהן's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause (one רגל is allowed, two means divorce) is about an ordinary Jewish woman. The later clause (three means divorce) gives more time because she is a כהנת. רבי יהודה is the תנא who gave a כהנת more time before divorce in an earlier משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of a משנה or ברייתא
'We have come to', meaning we are now dealing with a different case

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In the later clause, we have come to the wife of a kohen,
phrases.notes: The 'later clause' is the 'three רגלים, he must divorce' line from step 19.

phrases.english: and it follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 19 between the two clauses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split the cases: the two clauses talk about two different women (an ordinary wife and a כהנת).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses seemed to talk about the same woman, so they gave different answers for two רגלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two רגלים is grounds for divorce for an ordinary wife. A כהנת has until three, following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבה בר עולא: Eager woman versus a woman who is not eager
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא gives a different answer: one clause is about a woman eager to visit her family, and the other is about a woman who is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: It is not difficult. Here it is about a woman who is eager to visit; there it is about a woman who is not eager.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another way to answer the same contradiction. He splits the cases by how much the woman wants to visit her father's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a woman who is eager to visit home, more than one רגל is a real hardship, so two רגלים already means divorce. For a woman who is not eager, only a ban of three רגלים reaches that level. This answer works without bringing in a כהנת or רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult', the opening words of an answer
Eager, literally 'chased', meaning she really wants to go
'Here... there', used to split two sources into two different cases

steps.whyThisMatters: The word רדופה here leads straight into the next teaching about a bride who is eager to go to her father's house, and that is followed by a second teaching on the same theme.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said:
It is not difficult:
here it is about a woman who is eager,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the first clause, where one רגל is the limit.

phrases.english: there it is about a woman who is not eager.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא אָמַר, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בִּרְדוּפָה, כָּאן בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ רְדוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the same contradiction that אביי answered in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split the cases by the woman's personality: eager or not eager.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two clauses seemed to clash about two רגלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: For an eager woman, two רגלים means divorce. For a woman who is not eager, only three does.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the one-רגל versus three-רגלים clash. אביי says ordinary wife versus כהנת (רבי יהודה). רבה בר עולא says eager woman versus a woman who is not eager.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: A bride eager to tell her praise at home
steps.stepSummary: Because the word רדופה just came up, the גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's explanation of a פסוק about a bride eager to tell her family how well she is treated.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Then I was in his eyes as one who found peace.' רבי יוחנן said: Like a bride who is found perfect in her father-in-law's house, and is eager to go and tell her praise in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps aside from the הלכה to bring a teaching on a פסוק. It is linked to the word רדופה (eager) from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads 'שלום' as 'שלמה', meaning found perfect. The picture is a bride whose in-laws praise her, and she can't wait to go home and tell her family. This fits רבה בר עולא's idea that a wife can be eager to visit her father's house.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Finding peace', the words of the פסוק
Whole, perfect, found without any flaw
Her father-in-law's house, meaning her husband's family

phrases.english: "Then I was in his eyes as one who found peace"
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Like a bride who is found perfect in her father-in-law's house,
phrases.notes: He hears 'שלום' in the פסוק as 'שלמה', whole and without fault.

phrases.english: and is eager to go and tell her praise
in her father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אָז הָיִיתִי בְעֵינָיו כְּמוֹצְאֵת שָׁלוֹם״, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching linked by the word רדופה from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק describes a bride praised by her in-laws who is eager to report it to her own family.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'My husband' like a bride in her in-laws' house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the פסוק in הושע: the Jewish people will call ה׳‎ 'אישי' like a married bride in her in-laws' house, not 'בעלי' like a bride still in her father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it shall be on that day, says ה׳, you will call Me "My husband" and you will no longer call Me "My master".' רבי יוחנן said: Like a bride in her father-in-law's house, and not like a bride in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second teaching of רבי יוחנן about a bride. It also compares her father's house with her father-in-law's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bride who already lives with her husband feels close and calls him 'אישי', my husband. A bride who is only engaged and still lives at her father's house is more distant and calls him 'בעלי', my master. The פסוק promises a time of that kind of closeness between ה׳ and the Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: 'My husband', a close and personal name

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about the vow case. It is a side teaching about a פסוק, and the הלכה picks up again in the next step.

phrases.english: "And it shall be on that day, says ה׳,
you will call Me 'My husband'
and you will no longer call Me 'My master'"
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Like a bride in her father-in-law's house,
phrases.notes: He means a bride who is already married and living with her husband.

phrases.english: and not like a bride in her father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְהָיָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא נְאוּם ה׳ תִּקְרְאִי אִישִׁי וְלֹא תִקְרְאִי לִי עוֹד בַּעְלִי״, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי יוחנן on the same theme of a bride at her father's house versus her father-in-law's house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אישי' reflects the closeness of a married bride; 'בעלי' reflects the distance of a bride still in her father's house.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: banning his wife from a house of feasting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a husband who bans his wife from a בית האבל or a בית המשתה. It begins a question: the ban on a house of feasting makes sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who vows to forbid his wife...' etc. Granted, regarding a house of feasting...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה from step 17. It is setting up a question; it first grants that the house-of-feasting case is easy to understand, and the hard part comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא means 'I understand this part'. It tells you a contrast is coming: something else in the same line is harder to explain. The sentence is not finished yet and goes on past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: One who forbids someone through a vow
'Granted', meaning 'this part I understand', and a harder question comes next
A house of feasting, such as a wedding celebration

phrases.english: "One who vows to forbid his wife..." etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 17 about a בית האבל and a בית המשתה.

phrases.english: Granted, regarding a house of feasting,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְכוּ׳. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְבֵית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side teachings about the bride and goes back to the משנה's ruling in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Setting up a question on why each part of the משנה's ban counts as 'locking her in'. The house-of-feasting case is granted first, and the question itself follows.
